Folks — forwarding Cygnus' redlines. Short summary and suggested approach below. Please treat as priority.

Summary of asks (their phrasing):
1) Assignment of output ownership for outputs derived from Cygnus Content.
2) Training opt-out for subsets of customer data (sensitivity-based).
3) Broad perpetual feedback license for product improvement.

My initial take (fast):
- Assignment: We should not transfer general model ownership. We can offer assignment of "customer outputs" in a narrow sense (deliverables produced by customer content under the customer's guidance) or a time-limited exclusive license for productization. Full assignment of model weights/data is a non-starter.
- Training opt-out: feasible as a paid feature (managed opt-out flag + operational SLA). Need pricing from Ben and ops estimates from Olga.
- Feedback license: push to narrow scope and purpose (safety/bug fixes/operational telemetry), not broad product improvement that would let Cygnus claim derivative value. Consider making it irrevocable for a short duration only, or restricted to aggregated, de-identified telemetry.

Action items:
- Laura: propose redline language we can send back (snippets).
- Olga: ops impact & implementation notes + rough ETA and any telemetry tradeoffs.
- Ben: commercial note — pricing for training opt-out and any commitment needed for exclusive-license alternatives.

I'll aim to send a consolidated counter by EOD Tuesday. If legal wants quicker back-and-forth, please flag and I'll set a sync with Annika.

-Rafael

Rafael / team —

Thanks for the summary. Below are the redline proposals I recommend we send back to Cygnus; I've kept each recommendation short so procurement can copy/paste into their doc if needed.

1) Output ownership / assignment
- Proposal: Redwood will grant Customer an assignment of "Customer Outputs" as defined: "customer-authored prompts plus Customer Content provided to the Service and the outputs generated directly from that input, excluding any system prompts, Redwood proprietary model weights, or aggregated improvements."
- Alternative if they insist on broader rights: an exclusive, assignable license for Customer Outputs for a term of 24 months limited to Customer's productization of those outputs. After 24 months, rights revert to Redwood (or convert to a perpetual non-exclusive license).
- Rationale: assignment of raw model or training-derived weights is not acceptable; this language protects Redwood IP while satisfying customers who need productization rights.

2) Training opt-out (sensitivity carveout)
- Proposal: include Order Form checkbox / Exhibit for "Training Opt-Out" that applies only to data marked as "Sensitive Customer Data" in Exhibit X. Redwood will implement a technical flag to exclude flagged data from model training and product improvement pools. This is offered as a paid add-on; list pricing in the Order Form (Ben to provide).
- Evidence & audit: Customer must provide an inventory and classification of datasets subject to opt-out. Redwood will provide attestations per quarter but will not expose raw logs.

3) Feedback license
- Proposal: narrow the license to: "Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated feedback and telemetry to: (i) maintain and operate the Service, (ii) improve safety, and (iii) fix bugs. Redwood will not use such Feedback to train models for commercial general-purpose product improvements without Customer's explicit opt-in."
- Add carveout: allow Redwood to use anonymized telemetry for benchmarking and capacity planning.

4) Escrow / evidence path (operational)
- Add a short clause: if Customer requires full assignment for a specific deliverable, accept only with escrowed evidence of Customer IP provenance and an indemnity carveout.

Next steps / deadline:
- If acceptable, I suggest we send this draft back as tracked suggestions and propose a 30-minute legal-to-legal call on Wed (my calendar is open 10:30–12:30 PT).

Ben / Olga — please provide the pricing estimate and ops impact by EOD Tuesday so we can include Exhibit language.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
